issues.legal_issue: Coercive recovery against the property of an industrial company undergoing rehabilitation is suspended while the statutory inquiry or scheme process is pending, unless the competent authority consents.
material_facts: The company had been declared a sick industrial company after an inquiry.
The Board found that the company could not make its net worth positive within a reasonable time and appointed an operating agency to prepare a rehabilitation or revival scheme.
A local authority initiated coercive proceedings to recover property tax and other dues from the company’s property.
The local authority had not obtained the Board’s consent to proceed with recovery.
The High Court quashed the recovery proceedings, and the local authority sought leave to challenge that decision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in quashing the recovery proceedings; such proceedings against the company’s property could not proceed without the Board’s consent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 16 and 17(2)–(3) of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985, the Board may inquire into whether an industrial company is sick and direct preparation of a rehabilitation scheme. Under Section 22(1), while the specified inquiry or scheme process is pending, proceedings for execution, distress or the like against the company’s property may not be instituted or continued without the consent of the Board or appellate authority. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: special_leave_challenge_to_quashed_recovery and rehabilitation_process_pending and coercive_recovery_against_company_property and not authority_consent

predicates.special_leave_challenge_to_quashed_recov: A party sought special leave to challenge a decision quashing recovery proceedings against an industrial company.
predicates.rehabilitation_process_pending: The company had been found sick and an inquiry or rehabilitation-scheme process concerning it was pending.
predicates.coercive_recovery_against_company_proper: A creditor or public authority initiated or continued coercive proceedings to recover a debt from the company’s property.
predicates.authority_consent: The competent authority consented to the recovery proceedings.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns quashed recovery proceedings and a rehabilitation process is pending, coercive recovery against company property without authority consent is suspended.

issues.legal_issue: Suspension of a creditor’s recovery remedy during the rehabilitation process postpones the remedy rather than extinguishing it, and the suspension period is excluded when computing limitation for enforcing the right.
material_facts: The local authority had a claim for property tax and other dues against the company.
The company’s recovery proceedings were suspended because the statutory rehabilitation process was underway and the Board had not consented to recovery.
The Court observed that the creditor could seek the Board’s approval and that the limitation period would exclude the period during which the remedy remained suspended.
issues.conclusion: If approval is not granted, the creditor’s remedy is postponed rather than extinguished, and the suspension period is excluded when computing limitation for recovery.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22(5) of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 provides that the period during which a right or its enforcement remedy remains suspended under that section is excluded when computing limitation. The Court read this provision together with the suspension under Section 22(1). The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.creditor_recovery_claim_under_suspension: A creditor’s claim for payment was subject to suspended enforcement proceedings.
predicates.rehabilitation_process_pending: The company had been found sick and an inquiry or rehabilitation-scheme process concerning it was pending.
predicates.authority_consent_denied: The competent authority did not consent to the creditor proceeding with recovery.

issues.definition: When a creditor’s recovery claim is suspended during a pending rehabilitation process and consent to proceed is denied, the remedy survives and the suspension time is excluded from limitation.
